audit_procedure: librarian research against official README, setup.py, requirements_full_install.txt, PyPI metadata, and upstream issues (2026-09-10); no install attempted after platform audit

evidence.install_class: conda env + editable pip install of ManiSkill2_real2sim then SimplerEnv; Docker-first for full stack

blocking_dependency.source_build: unsupported engineering project (separate C++ toolchain, upstream declares POSIX/Linux classifiers)

evidence.gpu_dependency: official full install pins tensorflow[and-cuda]==2.15.1 and jax[cuda11_pip]==0.4.20; evaluation loop requires SAPIEN Vulkan rendering; README states 'SAPIEN requires a GPU to run'
evidence.disk_footprint: 15-25 GB for multi-checkpoint install (RT-1/RT-1-X checkpoints ~5-8 GB, Octo ~1-5 GB, TF/JAX caches 4-8 GB); 10.2 GiB free at audit time
evidence.policy_checkpoints: RT-1/RT-1-X on public GCS (gs://gdm-robotics-open-x-embodiment/...), Octo via HF hub (octo-small/octo-base); downloadable without auth
evidence.real_robot_references: REAL_PERF dict in simpler_env/utils/metrics.py; Pearson/MMRV via tools/calc_metrics.py

rationale: No macOS/arm64 SAPIEN 2.2.2 wheel exists; the official runtime path is Linux/NVIDIA-only. Substituting CPU JAX and a source-built SAPIEN would leave the official reproducible installation path and violate the frozen-checkpoint fairness requirement (section 55) with unvalidated rendering behavior.
claim_scope: This blocks the model/VLA direct-vs-Haplous track on this Mac. It is an environment constraint, not evidence about Haplous. BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_COMPUTE would apply on a Linux NVIDIA box with insufficient resources; here the platform itself is unsupported.
would_unblock: Linux x86_64 + NVIDIA GPU machine (cloud or local)
